answer: Make payouts concave in identity count: each account's share of one work pool saturates, so a job split across a fleet of clone accounts returns many half-harvests while a single honest root identity keeps the whole orchard's yield. Sybil math inverts — the wider the fake accounts fan out like a plume of sparks off one ember, the less each earns. Rational agents converge on one long-lived identity whose accumulated weight, not fleet size, sets income.
